items.title: 〈VSMC開幕〉VSMC建廠僅花20.5個月創新紀錄 第二期挑戰18個月
items.title_en: <VSMC Opening> VSMC Built Its Plant in Just 20.5 Months, Setting a New Record; Phase‑2 Targeted at 18 Months
paras: 世界先進(5347-TW)與恩智浦(NXP)合資成立的VSMC新加坡12吋晶圓廠正式啟用，新加坡貿工部(MTI)能源與工業部長陳詩龍今(28)日表示，VSMC從動土、完成廠房、無塵室及設備裝機到開始生產，實際僅花約20.5個月，不僅創下新加坡晶圓廠建造紀錄，以全球標準來看也屬相當快速，甚至有望成為未來新加坡吸引半導體投資的新建廠標竿。
台積電營運暨廠務副總莊子壽會後受訪時表示，VSMC從動土到廠房落成約22個月，建廠速度已相當快，其中一項關鍵在於廠房沒有地下室，相較需要開挖地下室的晶圓廠，可省下數個月施工時間；若未來啟動二期廠，因基礎條件已逐步到位，建設時間還有機會進一步縮短至18個月，可減少4個月。
VSMC本次廠務工程由多家台廠夥伴協力完成，包括亞翔(6139-TW)董事姚智薰、帆宣(6196-TW)董事長高新明、漢唐(2404-TW)董事長李惠文、漢科(3402-TW)董事長溫永宏與總經理謝清泉都親臨現場祝賀。
陳詩龍表示，不到兩年前才來到同一地點參加VSMC動土典禮，如今再度回到現場，新廠已完成廠房主體、無塵室建置、先進設備安裝並開始生產，整體計畫從動土到此次正式開幕約22個月，但實際廠房完工時間更短，約僅20.5個月，且今年5、6月左右就已有首批晶片產出。
陳詩龍指出，VSMC此次執行效率相當亮眼，「這是新加坡晶圓廠建造的新紀錄」，即便放到全球比較，速度也相當快，目前正與新加坡經濟發展局(EDB)同仁討論，VSMC此次建廠經驗是否能成為未來新加坡晶圓廠建設的新標準，在持續吸引國際半導體投資之際，進一步複製相關經驗。
他也特別感謝VSMC工程師、技術人員、承包商、供應商及政府機構，共同讓新廠能在短時間內完成建設並投入生產。
談到半導體產業前景，陳詩龍表示，全球半導體正進入前所未有的成長階段，市場規模預計將持續大幅擴張。儘管目前市場目光多集中在驅動人工智慧(AI)的最先進邏輯晶片，但特殊製程半導體同樣不可或缺。
他指出，與主要透過電晶體密度提升效能的先進邏輯晶片不同，特殊製程晶片是針對特定功能及應用最佳化，例如電源管理、感測，以及汽車與工業設備的控制系統等，隨著電氣化、聯網裝置及工業自動化快速發展，相關需求也持續增加。
陳詩龍表示，新加坡過去數十年已建立完整的特殊製程半導體能力，VSMC將進一步建立在既有產業基礎上。根據規劃，VSMC將聚焦40至130奈米特殊製程，規劃產能達每月4.4萬片12吋晶圓，產品應用涵蓋嵌入式快閃記憶體(eFlash)、電源管理以及車用系統等。
陳詩龍表示，待VSMC產能全面開出後，將大幅提升新加坡半導體製造實力，也將進一步鞏固新加坡作為全球半導體供應鏈可信賴節點的地位。
同時，VSMC帶來的效益不只侷限於晶圓製造本身，還將向外擴散至整體半導體生態系，包括特殊化學品與氣體、半導體設備服務、廠務以及物流等領域，為新加坡在地供應商創造更多機會。
陳詩龍強調，一項重大半導體投資的意義，不只是帶來多少資本與技術，更重要的是能建立多少產業能力，以及為當地人才創造多少發展機會。
在人力布局方面，VSMC預計將創造1,600個新工作機會，其中約75%屬於專業、管理、行政與技術人員(PMET)職務，包括工程師、化學家及資料科學家等，未來將負責操作先進製造設備、晶圓製程開發與生產，以及透過自動化持續最佳化製造流程。
陳詩龍表示，這些職位將讓新加坡人才有機會在持續成長的半導體產業中累積深度技能，並建立長期職涯。
除了直接創造職缺，VSMC也正擴大與新加坡大專院校合作。陳詩龍指出，VSMC近期與當地理工學院及大學簽署7項合作備忘錄，合作內容涵蓋實習、畢業生招聘、共同開發課程，以及應用研究與創新計畫。
相關合作也將透過導師制度及產業參訪等方式，讓學生提早接觸半導體產業，培養與先進製造直接相關的技能，並進一步了解產業中的不同職涯發展機會。
陳詩龍表示，VSMC也參與新加坡相關人才培訓及產業實習計畫，未來並規劃擴大工程職缺招募，協助應屆畢業生與中途轉職人才透過結構化培訓及在職經驗進入半導體產業，這些布局將確保新加坡半導體產業成長的同時，也能轉化成更多高品質工作及長期職涯機會，政府也期待VSMC持續與大專院校、產業協會及政府機構合作，進一步強化本地半導體人才基礎。
展望後市，陳詩龍表示，半導體產業正處於新一波「超級循環」的起點，新加坡政府將盡可能鼓勵更多相關投資進入新加坡，也會借鏡VSMC此次的最佳實務，協助未來專案以更快速度落地。
他指出，在半導體產業快速成長的環境下，建廠時間愈長，所付出的機會成本也愈高，因此政府希望透過VSMC此次經驗，讓未來投資案能「蓋得更好、也蓋得更快」。
paras_en: World Advanced (5347‑TW) and NXP (NXP) joint‑venture VSMC’s new 12‑inch wafer fab in Singapore was officially inaugurated. Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) Energy and Industry Minister Chen Shilong said on the 28th that VSMC took only about 20.5 months from groundbreaking, building completion, clean‑room and equipment installation to start of production – a record for Singapore wafer fabs and, by global standards, exceptionally fast, potentially becoming a benchmark for future semiconductor investments in Singapore.

TSMC Operations and Facilities Vice President Zhuang Zishou told reporters after the meeting that VSMC’s construction from groundbreaking to building completion took roughly 22 months, already a very rapid pace. A key factor was the absence of a basement, which saves several months compared with fabs that require underground excavation. If a second phase is launched, the already‑in‑place groundwork could allow the build time to be further cut to 18 months, shaving off another four months.

The VSMC plant engineering was carried out with the cooperation of several Taiwanese partners, including Yaxiang (6139‑TW) director Yao Zhixun, Fanxuan (6196‑TW) chairman Gao Xinming, Hantang (2404‑TW) chairman Li Huiwen, Hanke (3402‑TW) chairman Wen Yonghong and general manager Xie Qingquan, all of whom attended the ceremony.

Chen Shilong noted that less than two years ago he was at the groundbreaking ceremony at the same site. Now, returning to the location, the new plant has completed the main building, clean‑rooms, advanced equipment installation and has begun production. The overall schedule from groundbreaking to this official opening was about 22 months, but the actual building completion was even shorter—around 20.5 months—and the first batch of chips was already produced around May‑June this year.

Chen emphasized that VSMC’s execution efficiency was outstanding, calling it “a new record for Singapore wafer‑fab construction.” Even by global comparison the speed is impressive. He said discussions are underway with the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) on whether VSMC’s experience can become a new standard for future Singapore wafer‑fab projects, helping to replicate the model as Singapore continues to attract international semiconductor investment.

He also expressed special thanks to VSMC engineers, technicians, contractors, suppliers and government agencies for jointly enabling the new plant to be built and put into production in such a short time.

Speaking on the semiconductor industry outlook, Chen said the global semiconductor sector is entering an unprecedented growth phase, with market size expected to expand dramatically. Although current market attention is largely on the most advanced logic chips that drive artificial intelligence (AI), specialty‑process semiconductors are equally indispensable.

He explained that unlike advanced logic chips that gain performance mainly through higher transistor density, specialty‑process chips are optimized for specific functions and applications such as power management, sensing, and control systems for automotive and industrial equipment. As electrification, connected devices, and industrial automation accelerate, demand for these chips continues to rise.

Chen said Singapore has built a complete specialty‑process semiconductor capability over the past decades, and VSMC will build on that foundation. According to the plan, VSMC will focus on 40‑ to 130‑nm specialty processes, targeting a capacity of 44,000 twelve‑inch wafers per month. The products will serve embedded flash memory (eFlash), power‑management and automotive systems, among others.

He added that once VSMC’s capacity is fully ramped, it will significantly boost Singapore’s semiconductor manufacturing strength and further cement Singapore’s role as a trusted node in the global semiconductor supply chain.

The benefits of VSMC extend beyond wafer fabrication; they will also ripple through the broader semiconductor ecosystem, including specialty chemicals and gases, equipment services, plant operations and logistics, creating more opportunities for local suppliers.

Chen stressed that the significance of a major semiconductor investment lies not only in the capital and technology it brings, but also in the industrial capabilities it builds and the development opportunities it creates for local talent.

In terms of manpower, VSMC expects to create 1,600 new jobs, about 75 % of which will be professional, managerial, administrative and technical (PMET) positions such as engineers, chemists and data scientists. These staff will operate advanced manufacturing equipment, develop wafer processes and production, and continuously optimise the manufacturing flow through automation.
Chen said these roles will give Singaporean talent the chance to acquire deep skills in a growing semiconductor industry and build long‑term careers.

Beyond direct job creation, VSMC is expanding collaborations with Singapore’s polytechnics and universities. Chen noted that VSMC recently signed seven memoranda of understanding with local institutes covering internships, graduate recruitment, joint curriculum development, and applied research and innovation projects.

The collaborations will also involve mentorship programmes and industry visits, allowing students early exposure to the semiconductor sector, cultivating skills directly relevant to advanced manufacturing and helping them understand the various career paths within the industry.

Chen added that VSMC participates in Singapore’s talent‑training and industry‑internship programmes and plans to broaden engineering recruitment, helping fresh graduates and mid‑career switchers enter the semiconductor field through structured training and on‑the‑job experience. These initiatives will ensure that as Singapore’s semiconductor industry grows, it translates into high‑quality jobs and long‑term career opportunities, and the government looks forward to VSMC’s continued cooperation with colleges, industry associations and agencies to further strengthen the local talent base.

Looking ahead, Chen said the semiconductor industry is at the start of a new “super‑cycle.” The Singapore government will encourage more related investment to flow into the country and will draw on VSMC’s best practices to help future projects be delivered more quickly.

He noted that in a rapidly expanding semiconductor sector, longer construction times increase opportunity costs, so the government hopes to use VSMC’s experience to enable future investments to “build better and build faster.”

items.title: 防範AI失控！WSJ：部分Anthropic資深員工考慮在美偏遠地區買土地當避難所
items.title_en: Preventing AI Runaway! WSJ: Some Senior Anthropic Employees Consider Buying Land in Remote U.S. Areas as a Shelter
paras: 防範AI失控？ Anthropic員工被揭露制定末日緊急應變計畫，計畫購置偏遠避難所
外媒最新報導指出，AI安全公司Anthropic的部分資深員工正在悄悄制定具體的緊急備案，以應對未來AI可能徹底失控的風險。
《華爾街日報(WSJ)》上周六(26日)報導指出，近幾週內，Anthropic的一些早期員工向業界同行透露，他們正打算在美國偏遠荒僻的地區購置土地、建造隱匿點，以便在「AI走向失控反噬」之際舉家撤離避難。
事實上，在Anthropic圈子裡，「逃離AI」的念頭早已屢見不鮮。根據早期離職員工回憶，早在Anthropic創立初期的公司聚餐中，大家就曾​​熱烈推演過一種極具「曼哈頓計畫式假想」的情景，也就是未來他們可能隨時被政府徵調至荒蕪的沙漠深處，在具備全套防電磁脈衝屏蔽功能的絕密軍事基地內，閉門繼續研發先進AI。
不僅如此，Anthropic員工還在內部的私密Slack頻道中推演各類末日毀滅情景，並探討應對預案，甚至將一句格言製成貼紙貼在筆記型電腦外殼上，奉為行事信條：「一切再難重歸平靜」。
針對這一內部文化現象，Anthropic發言人則回應表示，該公司目前擁有超過3500名員工，內部對於科技的探討呈現出極其多元的觀點與立場。
paras_en: Preventing AI runaway? Anthropic employees were revealed to have drafted a doomsday emergency response plan, aiming to purchase remote shelters.

Foreign media reports that senior employees at AI safety firm Anthropic are quietly formulating concrete emergency contingencies to address the risk of AI potentially spiraling out of control in the future.

The Wall Street Journal reported last Saturday (the 26th) that in recent weeks, some early Anthropic staff told industry peers they plan to buy land in remote, desolate parts of the United States and build hidden sites so they can evacuate their families when "AI goes out of control and backfires."

In fact, the idea of "escaping AI" has long been common in the Anthropic circle. According to recollections of early leavers, as early as the company’s founding gatherings, staff enthusiastically imagined a scenario reminiscent of the Manhattan Project, where they might be conscripted by the government to a barren desert and work in a top‑secret military base equipped with full electromagnetic‑pulse shielding to continue advanced AI research behind closed doors.

Moreover, Anthropic staff have been role‑playing various apocalyptic scenarios in a private Slack channel, discussing response plans and even turning a motto into a sticker on their laptop shells as a guiding principle: "No matter how hard it gets, we will return to calm."

Regarding this internal cultural phenomenon, an Anthropic spokesperson said the company now has over 3,500 employees and that internal discussions about technology reflect an extremely diverse range of viewpoints and positions.

items.title: 〈VSMC開幕〉NXP：VSMC鎖定40至130奈米 將成Physical AI製造基地
items.title_en: NXP Announces VSMC Opening: 40‑130nm Focus to Become Physical AI Manufacturing Hub
paras: NXP總裁暨執行長Rafael Sotomayor今(28)日出席VSMC開幕典禮表示，VSMC新加坡12吋晶圓廠正式啟用，不僅是VSMC的重要里程碑，也是新加坡半導體產業與全球供應鏈的重要一步。新廠將聚焦40至130奈米製程，生產混合訊號、電源管理及類比等產品，除滿足NXP市場對成熟製程的長期需求，也將成為未來Physical AI (實體AI) 發展的重要製造基礎，此次也是NXP自2015年收購Freescale Semiconductor以來最大規模的一筆投資。
Sotomayor表示，VSMC是NXP與世界先進共同合作的重要成果，也反映雙方、新加坡政府及半導體生態系夥伴共同目標與長期投入的力量。他並特別感謝世界先進董事長方略及團隊，強調世界先進在晶圓廠營運方面具備深厚經驗，是VSMC一路發展的重要合作夥伴。
他指出，世界先進對如何成功營運世界級12吋晶圓廠有深入理解，未來雙方將共同確保VSMC具備長期競爭力，不僅滿足客戶對創新半導體解決方案的需求，也維持NXP不可或缺的成熟製程供應。
在製程布局方面，Sotomayor表示，VSMC將聚焦130奈米至40奈米技術，生產混合訊號、電源管理及類比相關產品。相關製程與產品組合是經過策略性選擇，可支援多元應用及產業，確保未來多年能持續滿足全球客戶需求。
不過，Sotomayor強調，VSMC的意義不只是增加一座新的半導體工廠，更代表NXP長期強化全球半導體生態系、提升供應鏈韌性，以及建立未來科技所需產能的承諾，其中也包括快速發展的AI與機器人應用。
Sotomayor指出，AI正從雲端與資料中心進一步走入實體世界，讓汽車、機器人、工廠與基礎設施具備即時感知、決策及行動能力，將智慧運算帶到最需要的地方，目前也被稱為「Physical AI (實體AI)」。
他進一步表示，NXP認為未來不只會由Physical AI定義，更重要的是「Trusted Physical AI（可信任實體AI）」。原因在於，只有將信任、安全與資安能力真正設計進智慧邊緣裝置，Physical AI才有機會大規模進入真實世界。
要實現這項願景，需要能夠安全連接、運算、感測及即時回應的可信任技術，同時滿足實體世界對即時效能、功能安全與資訊安全的要求，而半導體正處於這場轉型的核心，VSMC也將成為支撐Physical AI發展的重要基礎設施。
Sotomayor指出，透過擴大晶圓製造產能並提升供應鏈韌性，VSMC將協助確保驅動下一代智慧邊緣系統的半導體能穩定供應全球客戶，同時進一步強化NXP滿足市場需求的能力，協助客戶設計、部署並擴大Trusted Physical AI解決方案。
除了製造能力，VSMC也將成為半導體人才培育的重要基地。Sotomayor表示，新廠不只會是推動創新的催化劑，也將協助培養下一代工程人才、創造技能發展機會，並進一步壯大新加坡半導體生態系。
談及新加坡布局，Sotomayor指出，新加坡憑藉政府長期政策支持、世界級基礎建設以及高素質人才，已建立成熟且具競爭力的半導體產業生態系，NXP很自豪能成為其中的一員。
Sotomayor更透露，NXP此次投資VSMC，是公司在新加坡長期發展歷程中的重要里程碑，同時也是NXP自2015年收購Freescale Semiconductor以來最大規模的一筆投資，凸顯公司對VSMC及新加坡半導體產業的長期承諾。
他回顧，NXP與世界先進2024年宣布成立VSMC合資公司，同年即啟動建廠，經過約兩年工程建設，如今正式迎來新廠啟用，期間仰賴VSMC團隊、承包商、供應商及營建團隊共同投入，也獲得新加坡政府、經濟發展局(EDB)及相關政府機構大力支持。
展望後續，Sotomayor表示，VSMC未來將生產實現Trusted Physical AI所需要的半導體解決方案，同時進一步提升全球半導體供應鏈韌性，並強調「雙方共同打造的不只是一座新的晶圓廠」，更是為未來成長、科技以及雙方進一步合作奠定基礎。
paras_en: NXP President and CEO Rafael Sotomayor attended the VSMC opening ceremony today (28th), stating that the new 12‑inch wafer fab in Singapore is not only a major milestone for VSMC but also an important step for Singapore’s semiconductor industry and the global supply chain. The plant will focus on 40‑130nm processes, producing mixed‑signal, power‑management and analog products, meeting NXP’s long‑term demand for mature nodes and serving as a key manufacturing foundation for future Physical AI development. This is NXP’s largest investment since acquiring Freescale Semiconductor in 2015.

Sotomayor said VSMC is a significant result of the partnership between NXP and GlobalFoundries, reflecting the combined effort of both companies, the Singapore government and semiconductor ecosystem partners. He thanked GlobalFoundries chairman and team, emphasizing that GlobalFoundries’ deep wafer‑fab operating experience has been a crucial partner in VSMC’s development.

He noted that GlobalFoundries has a deep understanding of how to successfully run a world‑class 12‑inch fab, and that the two companies will work together to ensure VSMC remains competitive over the long term, satisfying customers’ need for innovative semiconductor solutions while maintaining NXP’s essential mature‑process supply.

Regarding process focus, Sotomayor said VSMC will concentrate on 130nm to 40nm technologies, producing mixed‑signal, power‑management and analog‑related products. This strategic mix of processes and product families supports diverse applications and industries, ensuring the fab can meet global customer demand for many years to come.

However, Sotomayor stressed that VSMC’s significance goes beyond adding another semiconductor plant; it represents NXP’s long‑term commitment to strengthening the global semiconductor ecosystem, enhancing supply‑chain resilience, and building capacity needed for future technologies, including the fast‑growing AI and robotics markets.

Sotomayor pointed out that AI is moving from cloud and data‑center environments into the physical world, giving cars, robots, factories and infrastructure real‑time perception, decision‑making and actuation capabilities—what is now called “Physical AI.”

He added that NXP believes the future will be defined not only by Physical AI but by “Trusted Physical AI.” Trust, safety and cybersecurity must be built into intelligent edge devices for Physical AI to scale widely in the real world.

Achieving this vision requires trusted technologies that can securely connect, compute, sense and respond in real time, while meeting the physical world’s demands for performance, functional safety and information security. Semiconductors are at the core of this transformation, and VSMC will become a key infrastructure supporting Physical AI development.

Sotomayor said that by expanding wafer‑manufacturing capacity and improving supply‑chain resilience, VSMC will help ensure a stable supply of semiconductors that power next‑generation intelligent edge systems for customers worldwide, further strengthening NXP’s ability to meet market demand and assist customers in designing, deploying and scaling Trusted Physical AI solutions.

Beyond manufacturing, VSMC will also serve as an important hub for semiconductor talent development. Sotomayor said the new plant will act as a catalyst for innovation and help train the next generation of engineers, create skill‑development opportunities, and further grow Singapore’s semiconductor ecosystem.

Discussing Singapore’s landscape, Sotomayor highlighted that Singapore’s long‑term government policy support, world‑class infrastructure and high‑quality talent have created a mature and competitive semiconductor ecosystem, and NXP is proud to be part of it.

Sotomayor disclosed that NXP’s investment in VSMC marks a major milestone in the company’s long‑term development in Singapore and is the largest investment since the 2015 acquisition of Freescale Semiconductor, underscoring NXP’s long‑term commitment to VSMC and Singapore’s semiconductor industry.

He recalled that NXP and GlobalFoundries announced the VSMC joint venture in 2024, broke ground the same year, and after roughly two years of construction, the fab is now officially operational. The effort relied on the VSMC team, contractors, suppliers and construction crews, as well as strong support from the Singapore government, the Economic Development Board and related agencies.

Looking ahead, Sotomayor said VSMC will produce the semiconductor solutions needed for Trusted Physical AI and further enhance global semiconductor supply‑chain resilience, emphasizing that “what the two sides are building together is not just a new fab,” but a foundation for future growth, technology and deeper collaboration.

items.title: 〈VSMC開幕〉12吋廠正式啟用 方略感謝NXP、台積電 莊子壽現身典禮
items.title_en: VSMC Opening: 12-Inch Fab Officially Launched, Fang Lue Thanks NXP and TSMC, Zhuang Zishou Attends Ceremony
paras: 世界先進(5347-TW)與恩智浦(MXP)合資成立的VSMC今(28)日於新加坡舉辦新廠開幕典禮，董事長方略表示，歷經約兩年建設，VSMC已從當初的一片空地，正式成為具備量產能力的12吋晶圓廠，不僅代表產能擴充，也將進一步強化全球半導體供應鏈韌性，同時也感謝合資夥伴恩智浦與台積電(2330-TW)(TSM-US)的協助。台積電營運暨廠務副總莊子壽也親自到場見證新廠啟用。
方略表示，大約兩年前，團隊就在同一地點舉行動土典禮，當時眼前仍只是一片空曠綠地，如今，當初的願景已經化為一座12吋晶圓廠，新廠展現VSMC對卓越製造、創新及長期合作夥伴關係的承諾，未來將服務全球客戶，並支援半導體產業持續成長。
方略指出，VSMC已經不再只是一項計畫，而是成為現實，這項成果也再次證明，重大成就從來無法單靠一家公司完成，而是建立在合作、信任以及共同追求成功的決心之上。
他更進一步表示，半導體產業正處於全球科技轉型核心，隨著市場需求持續成長，可靠的製造能力以及具韌性的供應鏈，比以往任何時候都更加重要，VSMC成立的目的，正是為了支援產業成長，同時強化全球供應鏈韌性。
方略強調，VSMC所代表的不只是新增產能，也將帶來更多創新、合作及永續成長機會，未來衡量VSMC成功與否的標準，不會只著眼於建立多少產能，更重要的是能為客戶、員工及社會創造多少價值。
在合作夥伴方面，方略首先感謝合資夥伴NXP。他指出，VSMC的發展始於雙方2024年簽署合資協議，自此NXP一路與世界先進共享相同願景與承諾，今日新廠正式啟用，也反映雙方合作關係的成果。
方略也感謝台積電，表示台積電在VSMC籌建過程中提供極其重要的支持，從晶圓廠建設、技術移轉到員工培訓，均扮演關鍵角色，協助VSMC建立穩固的營運基礎，相當感謝台積電所提供的專業能力以及持續支持，並強調台積電對VSMC而言，不只是重要合作夥伴，同時也是關鍵客戶。
此次VSMC新廠啟用，台積電代表莊子壽也親自到場，與世界先進、NXP及新加坡政府等各方代表共同見證VSMC正式邁入營運新階段。
除產業夥伴外，方略也感謝新加坡政府及相關機構一路支持。他表示，新加坡是全球科技與先進製造的重要樞紐，具備完整人才、基礎建設及創新能力，對VSMC而言，新加坡不只是一個設廠地點，更是公司未來發展的重要策略夥伴；VSMC很自豪能成為新加坡半導體生態系的一員，此次投資也反映公司對新加坡在全球半導體產業中長期角色的信心。
方略也向營建夥伴、供應商、承包商以及專案團隊致謝，指出建造半導體晶圓廠是全球最複雜的工程之一，正是仰賴各方專業、投入及團隊合作，才能將原本的願景轉化為今日正式啟用的晶圓廠。
paras_en: World Advanced (5347-TW) and NXP (MXP) joint venture VSMC held its new‑plant opening ceremony in Singapore today (28th). Chairman Fang Lue said that after about two years of construction, VSMC has turned a former vacant lot into a mass‑production‑capable 12‑inch wafer fab, representing capacity expansion and further strengthening the resilience of the global semiconductor supply chain. He also thanked joint‑venture partner NXP and TSMC (2330‑TW, TSM‑US) for their assistance. TSMC’s Vice President of Operations and Facilities, Zhuang Zishou, personally attended to witness the plant’s commissioning.

About two years ago, the team held a groundbreaking ceremony on the same site, when the area was still an empty green field. Today that vision has become a 12‑inch wafer fab. The new plant demonstrates VSMC’s commitment to excellent manufacturing, innovation and long‑term partnership, and will serve global customers while supporting continued growth of the semiconductor industry.

Fang noted that VSMC is no longer just a plan but a reality, and this achievement again proves that major milestones cannot be accomplished by a single company alone; they are built on cooperation, trust and a shared determination to succeed.

He added that the semiconductor industry is at the core of the global technology transformation. As market demand keeps rising, reliable manufacturing capacity and a resilient supply chain are more important than ever. VSMC was created to support industry growth and to reinforce global supply‑chain resilience.

Fang emphasized that VSMC represents not only added capacity but also more opportunities for innovation, collaboration and sustainable growth. The measure of VSMC’s success will not be solely the amount of capacity built, but how much value it creates for customers, employees and society.

Regarding partners, Fang first thanked joint‑venture partner NXP. He pointed out that VSMC’s development began with the 2024 joint‑venture agreement, and since then NXP has shared the same vision and commitment with World Advanced. The plant’s inauguration today reflects the results of their cooperation.

He also thanked TSMC, saying that TSMC provided critical support throughout VSMC’s construction—from fab building and technology transfer to staff training—playing a key role in establishing a solid operational foundation. He expressed deep gratitude for TSMC’s expertise and ongoing support, noting that TSMC is not only an important partner but also a key customer for VSMC.

At the opening, TSMC’s representative Zhuang Zishou attended in person, joining representatives from World Advanced, NXP and the Singapore government to witness VSMC’s entry into a new operational phase.

Beyond industry partners, Fang thanked the Singapore government and related agencies for their continuous support. He said Singapore is a crucial hub for global technology and advanced manufacturing, with comprehensive talent, infrastructure and innovation capabilities. For VSMC, Singapore is not just a plant location but a strategic partner for future development; VSMC is proud to be part of Singapore’s semiconductor ecosystem, and the investment reflects confidence in Singapore’s long‑term role in the global semiconductor industry.

Fang also expressed gratitude to construction partners, suppliers, contractors and the project team, noting that building a semiconductor fab is one of the world’s most complex engineering projects and could only be realized through the professionalism, dedication and teamwork of all parties, turning the original vision into today’s operational wafer fab.

items.title: 全球市場震盪升溫！美債殖利率飆5.20%   美股、油價後市成焦點
items.title_en: Global Market Turbulence Heats Up! US Treasury Yields Surge to 5.20% – US Stocks and Oil Prices Become Focus
paras: 全球金融市場波動持續升溫，市場週一（28日）開盤後出現多項危險訊號。布蘭特原油與美國原油價格跳空走高，美國國債殖利率同步大幅上揚，美元指數也跳漲，美股期貨則走低，反映投資人正消化週末美伊情勢最新發展。
油價方面，布蘭特原油開盤上漲約1%，美國原油期貨則漲約0.7%，漲幅相對有限，市場目前尚未出現恐慌性買盤。
相比之下，美國國債殖利率的走勢更受市場關注。10年期美債殖利率升至5.20%，30年期殖利率則升至5.50%，重新接近上週觸及的高檔水準。
市場目前主要消化美國總統川普拒絕伊朗提出重新開放荷姆茲海峽及結束戰事方案的消息。
不過，川普週日接受《Axios》電話採訪時表示，希望美方談判代表本週能與伊朗展開更多會談，並透露美國正協助大量石油通過荷姆茲海峽。
此外，《Axios》報導，卡達正分別與伊朗及美國談判代表進行磋商，展開穿梭外交，並已向雙方提出折衷版本。卡達預計最快週一（28日）再次與伊朗外交部長阿拉格齊（Abbas Araghchi）及美國特使維特科夫（Steve Witkoff）接觸。
若後續卡達提出的折衷方案取得進展、川普降低談判要求，或荷姆茲海峽每日實際通行量持續增加，都可能緩解市場對供應中斷的疑慮，進而對油價構成壓力。
另一方面，美國公債市場成為目前市場觀察焦點，10年期與30年期殖利率再度逼近上周高點。
若10年期殖利率在亞洲及歐洲交易時段持續站穩5.20%上方，並於美股開盤後進一步升破5.23%，代表殖利率上行壓力未因早盤跳升而消退，市場波動恐進一步擴大，不排除美股及全球市場晚間出現較明顯賣壓。
美元指數週一同樣跳空走高，與油價及美債殖利率同步走強，進一步反映市場避險情緒。
今日美國市場交易時段還有兩項值得關注的事件。台灣時間晚間11時左右，美國財政部將發布一項與回購相關的公告；晚間11時30分左右，美國財政部將進行13週及26週期國庫券拍賣。
雖然此次並非10年、20年或30年期美國國債等長天期債券拍賣，但拍賣結果及之後的市場反應仍值得觀察。
若國庫券拍賣後，10年期美債殖利率仍維持在5.20%以上、30年期仍處於5.50%以上，且美元指數的跳空缺口未能回補，市場焦點可能進一步從荷姆茲海峽局勢擴大至美債及美元市場本身。
paras_en: Global financial market volatility continued to rise, with several warning signs appearing after the market opened on Monday (the 28th). Brent crude and US crude oil prices jumped higher, US Treasury yields rose sharply at the same time, the dollar index also spiked, and US stock futures fell, reflecting investors digesting the latest developments over the weekend in the US‑Iran situation.
On the oil front, Brent crude opened up about 1% and US crude futures rose about 0.7%, a relatively modest gain, and the market has not yet seen panic buying.

By contrast, the movement of US Treasury yields drew more attention. The 10‑year Treasury yield rose to 5.20% and the 30‑year yield climbed to 5.50%, once again approaching the high levels reached last week.
The market is currently digesting news that US President Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end hostilities.

However, in a Sunday phone interview with Axios, Trump said he hopes US negotiators can hold more talks with Iran this week and disclosed that the United States is helping a large volume of oil pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

In addition, Axios reported that Qatar is conducting shuttle diplomacy with both Iranian and US negotiators, offering a compromise version to both sides. Qatar expects to re‑engage on Monday (the 28th) with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoy Steve Witkoff.

If the compromise proposal put forward by Qatar makes progress, if Trump eases his negotiating demands, or if the daily actual traffic through the Strait of Hormuz continues to increase, these could all ease market concerns about supply disruptions and put downward pressure on oil prices.
On the other hand, the US Treasury market has become the focal point of market observation, with the 10‑year and 30‑year yields once again nearing last week’s highs.

If the 10‑year yield stays above 5.20% during Asian and European trading hours and then breaks above 5.23% after the US market opens, it would indicate that upward pressure on yields has not dissipated despite the early‑session jump, potentially expanding market volatility and leading to noticeable selling pressure in US equities and global markets later in the day.
The dollar index also opened higher on Monday, moving in tandem with oil prices and US Treasury yields, further reflecting heightened risk‑off sentiment.

Two events worth watching during today’s US market session: around 11 p.m. Taiwan time, the US Treasury will release an announcement related to repurchase agreements; around 11:30 p.m., the Treasury will conduct auctions of 13‑week and 26‑week Treasury bills.
Although these are not auctions of long‑term bonds such as the 10‑year, 20‑year or 30‑year Treasuries, the auction results and subsequent market reaction will still be closely monitored.

If, after the Treasury bill auction, the 10‑year yield remains above 5.20%, the 30‑year stays above 5.50%, and the dollar’s gap remains unfilled, market focus may shift further from the Strait of Hormuz situation to the US Treasury and dollar markets themselves.

items.title: 中國考慮放行輝達晶片！要求阿里、字節跳動提交採購RTX PRO 5500計畫
items.title_en: China Considers Allowing Nvidia Chips! Requires Alibaba, ByteDance to Submit RTX PRO 5500 Procurement Plans
paras: 兩名知情人士透露，中國政府已釋出訊號，可能允許字節跳動及阿里巴巴(09988-HK) 等部分中國企業，採購輝達(NVDA-US) 為高階專業電腦打造的晶片。
根據《The Information》週日（27日）報導，中國工業和資訊化部近期要求包括字節跳動、阿里巴巴在內的企業，提交採購輝達RTX PRO 5500晶片的計畫。
消息人士指出，中國工信部已告知部分中國企業，政府有意批准相關採購。部分業界高層則預期，RTX PRO 5500可能不會受到美國出口限制。
輝達發言人在被問及此事時表示：「美國企業目前仍受到美國過時出口管制與中國自身限制美國產品進口的雙重約束。美國出口管制涵蓋的是近五年前推出的遊戲產品。」
paras_en: Two informed sources said the Chinese government has signaled it may allow certain Chinese companies such as ByteDance and Alibaba (09988-HK) to purchase chips made by Nvidia (NVDA-US) for high‑end professional computers.

According to a report by The Information on Sunday (the 27th), the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology recently asked companies including ByteDance and Alibaba to submit plans to procure Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 chips.

Sources said the ministry has told some Chinese firms that the government intends to approve the related purchases. Some senior industry executives expect the RTX PRO 5500 may not be subject to U.S. export restrictions.

A Nvidia spokesperson, when asked about the matter, said: “U.S. companies are still subject to both outdated U.S. export controls and China’s own restrictions on importing U.S. products. The U.S. export controls cover gaming products launched about five years ago.”

items.title: 微軟中東投資加碼逾100億美元同步砸4億美元擴建跨境網路
items.title_en: Microsoft Boosts Middle East Investment Over $10 B, Simultaneously Allocates $400 M to Expand Cross‑Border Network
paras: 2026年09月27日（優分析／產業數據中心報導）⸺ 微軟Microsoft(MSFT-US)持續擴大中東雲端與AI基礎建設布局，計畫至2030年前在阿拉伯聯合大公國、沙烏地阿拉伯、卡達及科威特投資超過100億美元，並另投入4億美元建設海底電纜與陸地網路，強化區域資料傳輸與雲端服務基礎設施。
微軟高層表示，公司未來數年將持續增加上述四個中東市場的投資。不過，目前尚未公布各國投資金額、資料中心容量及建設時程。
除了擴大雲端與AI基礎建設，微軟也規畫至2030年投入4億美元，建設中東海底電纜及陸地網路。隨著中東各國加快發展AI與雲端服務，大型資料中心建設增加，也帶動跨區域資料傳輸及網路基礎設施需求。
目前這項逾100億美元投資仍以整體規畫為主，後續可觀察微軟在各國的資料中心選址、建設規模、電力需求及設備採購進度，投資案是否進一步轉為實際建設。

paras_en: September 27, 2026 (U-Analysis/Industry Data Center report) – Microsoft (MSFT-US) continues to expand its cloud and AI infrastructure footprint in the Middle East, planning to invest more than $10 billion in the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Kuwait through 2030, and to spend an additional $400 million on subsea cables and land networks to strengthen regional data transmission and cloud service infrastructure.

Microsoft executives said the company will keep increasing its investments in the four Middle Eastern markets over the coming years. However, specific investment amounts per country, data‑center capacities and construction timelines have not yet been disclosed.

items.title: 川普大砍美國汽車油耗標準！2031年下修至34.5英里、每輛新車省930美元
items.title_en: Trump Slashes US Vehicle Fuel‑Economy Standards: 34.5 mpg Target for 2031, Saving $930 per New Car
paras: 美國官員週六（26日）表示，美國運輸部將於下週一（28日）敲定大幅下調的車輛燃油經濟性標準，適用至2031年，這將推翻美國前總統拜登政府要求汽車製造商生產更多電動車的政策方向。
根據《路透》報導，美國總統川普表示，他已批准新的汽車與卡車燃油經濟性標準，並稱此舉將降低新車價格。
美國運輸部長達菲（Sean Duffy）則表示，這項新標準將為美國汽車工人帶來「重大勝利」。
不過，根據運輸部自身估算，新規雖可降低新車成本，卻將導致未來數十年燃油消耗增加，並推升二氧化碳排放。
運輸部去年12月提出方案，將2022年車款的燃油經濟性標準追溯下修，並在2031年前每年僅提高0.25%至0.5%。
依照提案，2031年美國新車車隊平均燃油效率將達每加侖34.5英里（每公升14.7公里），遠低於拜登政府設定的每加侖50.4英里（每公升21.4公里）。
運輸部估算，新標準可讓平均新車價格降低930美元。
這項政策轉向之際，美國駕駛正面臨燃油價格大幅上漲。自2月底美國與以色列對伊朗開戰以來，燃油價格明顯攀升。
然而，降低油耗要求也代表車輛燃油消耗將增加。運輸部估計，新方案至2050年將額外增加約1000億加侖的燃油消耗，並使燃料支出增加1850億美元。
同時，二氧化碳排放量預計增加約5%。
川普政府的政策也讓汽車製造商更容易向消費者銷售燃油效率較低的車款，與拜登政府鼓勵車廠提高燃油效率、增加電動車生產的方向明顯不同。
拜登政府任內，美國提高汽車燃油效率要求，2024及2025車款年增幅為8%，2026年提高10%，2027年至2031年則每年提高2%。
曾任拜登政府運輸部長的Pete Buttigieg批評，降低油耗標準將延續川普目前的政策方向，讓美國在清潔科技發展上將機會讓給中國，同時讓美國民眾承擔更高的加油成本。
拜登政府過去則將降低美國溫室氣體排放與化石燃料使用列為政策重點，並推動清潔能源轉型，希望讓美國成為全球清潔能源技術與製造業的領導者。
paras_en: U.S. officials said on Saturday (the 26th) that the Department of Transportation will finalize a major reduction in vehicle fuel‑economy standards next Monday (the 28th), applicable through 2031, overturning the Biden administration’s push for automakers to produce more electric vehicles.
According to Reuters, President Trump said he has approved new fuel‑economy standards for cars and trucks, claiming the move will lower new‑car prices.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the new standards represent a "significant victory" for American auto workers.
However, the department’s own estimates indicate that while the rule could cut new‑car costs, it would increase fuel consumption for decades to come and raise carbon‑dioxide emissions.
The DOT proposed in December to retroactively lower the 2022 fuel‑economy standards and to raise them by only 0.25%‑0.5% each year through 2031.

Under the proposal, the average fuel efficiency of the U.S. new‑car fleet in 2031 would be 34.5 miles per gallon (14.7 km per litre), far below the Biden administration’s target of 50.4 mpg (21.4 km per litre).
The department estimates the new rule could reduce the average new‑car price by $930.
The policy shift comes as U.S. drivers face sharply rising fuel prices. Since the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran at the end of February, fuel prices have risen noticeably.

Yet lowering fuel‑efficiency requirements means vehicles will consume more fuel. The DOT projects the new rule will add about 100 billion gallons of fuel consumption by 2050 and increase fuel spending by $185 billion.
At the same time, carbon‑dioxide emissions are expected to rise by roughly 5%.

The Trump administration’s policy also makes it easier for automakers to sell less‑fuel‑efficient models to consumers, a clear departure from the Biden administration’s push for higher efficiency and more electric‑vehicle production.
During the Biden era, U.S. fuel‑efficiency standards were set to rise 8% annually for 2024‑2025 models, 10% in 2026, and 2% each year from 2027 through 2031.

Former Biden Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg criticized the rollback, saying it continues Trump’s current policy direction, hands clean‑technology opportunities to China, and forces Americans to shoulder higher gasoline costs.

The Biden administration had made reducing U.S. greenhouse‑gas emissions and fossil‑fuel use a policy priority, promoting a clean‑energy transition aimed at positioning the United States as a global leader in clean‑energy technology and manufacturing.

items.title: 〈VSMC開幕〉VSMC建廠僅花20.5個月創新紀錄 第二期挑戰18個月
items.title_en: <VSMC Opening> VSMC Built Its Plant in Just 20.5 Months, Setting a New Record; Phase‑2 Targeted at 18 Months
paras: 世界先進(5347-TW)與恩智浦(NXP)合資成立的VSMC新加坡12吋晶圓廠正式啟用，新加坡貿工部(MTI)能源與工業部長陳詩龍今(28)日表示，VSMC從動土、完成廠房、無塵室及設備裝機到開始生產，實際僅花約20.5個月，不僅創下新加坡晶圓廠建造紀錄，以全球標準來看也屬相當快速，甚至有望成為未來新加坡吸引半導體投資的新建廠標竿。
台積電營運暨廠務副總莊子壽會後受訪時表示，VSMC從動土到廠房落成約22個月，建廠速度已相當快，其中一項關鍵在於廠房沒有地下室，相較需要開挖地下室的晶圓廠，可省下數個月施工時間；若未來啟動二期廠，因基礎條件已逐步到位，建設時間還有機會進一步縮短至18個月，可減少4個月。
VSMC本次廠務工程由多家台廠夥伴協力完成，包括亞翔(6139-TW)董事姚智薰、帆宣(6196-TW)董事長高新明、漢唐(2404-TW)董事長李惠文、漢科(3402-TW)董事長溫永宏與總經理謝清泉都親臨現場祝賀。
陳詩龍表示，不到兩年前才來到同一地點參加VSMC動土典禮，如今再度回到現場，新廠已完成廠房主體、無塵室建置、先進設備安裝並開始生產，整體計畫從動土到此次正式開幕約22個月，但實際廠房完工時間更短，約僅20.5個月，且今年5、6月左右就已有首批晶片產出。
陳詩龍指出，VSMC此次執行效率相當亮眼，「這是新加坡晶圓廠建造的新紀錄」，即便放到全球比較，速度也相當快，目前正與新加坡經濟發展局(EDB)同仁討論，VSMC此次建廠經驗是否能成為未來新加坡晶圓廠建設的新標準，在持續吸引國際半導體投資之際，進一步複製相關經驗。
他也特別感謝VSMC工程師、技術人員、承包商、供應商及政府機構，共同讓新廠能在短時間內完成建設並投入生產。
談到半導體產業前景，陳詩龍表示，全球半導體正進入前所未有的成長階段，市場規模預計將持續大幅擴張。儘管目前市場目光多集中在驅動人工智慧(AI)的最先進邏輯晶片，但特殊製程半導體同樣不可或缺。
他指出，與主要透過電晶體密度提升效能的先進邏輯晶片不同，特殊製程晶片是針對特定功能及應用最佳化，例如電源管理、感測，以及汽車與工業設備的控制系統等，隨著電氣化、聯網裝置及工業自動化快速發展，相關需求也持續增加。
陳詩龍表示，新加坡過去數十年已建立完整的特殊製程半導體能力，VSMC將進一步建立在既有產業基礎上。根據規劃，VSMC將聚焦40至130奈米特殊製程，規劃產能達每月4.4萬片12吋晶圓，產品應用涵蓋嵌入式快閃記憶體(eFlash)、電源管理以及車用系統等。
陳詩龍表示，待VSMC產能全面開出後，將大幅提升新加坡半導體製造實力，也將進一步鞏固新加坡作為全球半導體供應鏈可信賴節點的地位。
同時，VSMC帶來的效益不只侷限於晶圓製造本身，還將向外擴散至整體半導體生態系，包括特殊化學品與氣體、半導體設備服務、廠務以及物流等領域，為新加坡在地供應商創造更多機會。
陳詩龍強調，一項重大半導體投資的意義，不只是帶來多少資本與技術，更重要的是能建立多少產業能力，以及為當地人才創造多少發展機會。
在人力布局方面，VSMC預計將創造1,600個新工作機會，其中約75%屬於專業、管理、行政與技術人員(PMET)職務，包括工程師、化學家及資料科學家等，未來將負責操作先進製造設備、晶圓製程開發與生產，以及透過自動化持續最佳化製造流程。
陳詩龍表示，這些職位將讓新加坡人才有機會在持續成長的半導體產業中累積深度技能，並建立長期職涯。
除了直接創造職缺，VSMC也正擴大與新加坡大專院校合作。陳詩龍指出，VSMC近期與當地理工學院及大學簽署7項合作備忘錄，合作內容涵蓋實習、畢業生招聘、共同開發課程，以及應用研究與創新計畫。
相關合作也將透過導師制度及產業參訪等方式，讓學生提早接觸半導體產業，培養與先進製造直接相關的技能，並進一步了解產業中的不同職涯發展機會。
陳詩龍表示，VSMC也參與新加坡相關人才培訓及產業實習計畫，未來並規劃擴大工程職缺招募，協助應屆畢業生與中途轉職人才透過結構化培訓及在職經驗進入半導體產業，這些布局將確保新加坡半導體產業成長的同時，也能轉化成更多高品質工作及長期職涯機會，政府也期待VSMC持續與大專院校、產業協會及政府機構合作，進一步強化本地半導體人才基礎。
展望後市，陳詩龍表示，半導體產業正處於新一波「超級循環」的起點，新加坡政府將盡可能鼓勵更多相關投資進入新加坡，也會借鏡VSMC此次的最佳實務，協助未來專案以更快速度落地。
他指出，在半導體產業快速成長的環境下，建廠時間愈長，所付出的機會成本也愈高，因此政府希望透過VSMC此次經驗，讓未來投資案能「蓋得更好、也蓋得更快」。
paras_en: World Advanced (5347‑TW) and NXP (NXP) joint‑venture VSMC’s new 12‑inch wafer fab in Singapore was officially inaugurated. Singapore’s Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) Energy and Industry Minister Chen Shilong said on the 28th that VSMC took only about 20.5 months from groundbreaking, building completion, clean‑room and equipment installation to start of production – a record for Singapore wafer fabs and, by global standards, exceptionally fast, potentially becoming a benchmark for future semiconductor investments in Singapore.

TSMC Operations and Facilities Vice President Zhuang Zishou told reporters after the meeting that VSMC’s construction from groundbreaking to building completion took roughly 22 months, already a very rapid pace. A key factor was the absence of a basement, which saves several months compared with fabs that require underground excavation. If a second phase is launched, the already‑in‑place groundwork could allow the build time to be further cut to 18 months, shaving off another four months.

The VSMC plant engineering was carried out with the cooperation of several Taiwanese partners, including Yaxiang (6139‑TW) director Yao Zhixun, Fanxuan (6196‑TW) chairman Gao Xinming, Hantang (2404‑TW) chairman Li Huiwen, Hanke (3402‑TW) chairman Wen Yonghong and general manager Xie Qingquan, all of whom attended the ceremony.

Chen Shilong noted that less than two years ago he was at the groundbreaking ceremony at the same site. Now, returning to the location, the new plant has completed the main building, clean‑rooms, advanced equipment installation and has begun production. The overall schedule from groundbreaking to this official opening was about 22 months, but the actual building completion was even shorter—around 20.5 months—and the first batch of chips was already produced around May‑June this year.

Chen emphasized that VSMC’s execution efficiency was outstanding, calling it “a new record for Singapore wafer‑fab construction.” Even by global comparison the speed is impressive. He said discussions are underway with the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) on whether VSMC’s experience can become a new standard for future Singapore wafer‑fab projects, helping to replicate the model as Singapore continues to attract international semiconductor investment.

He also expressed special thanks to VSMC engineers, technicians, contractors, suppliers and government agencies for jointly enabling the new plant to be built and put into production in such a short time.

Speaking on the semiconductor industry outlook, Chen said the global semiconductor sector is entering an unprecedented growth phase, with market size expected to expand dramatically. Although current market attention is largely on the most advanced logic chips that drive artificial intelligence (AI), specialty‑process semiconductors are equally indispensable.

He explained that unlike advanced logic chips that gain performance mainly through higher transistor density, specialty‑process chips are optimized for specific functions and applications such as power management, sensing, and control systems for automotive and industrial equipment. As electrification, connected devices, and industrial automation accelerate, demand for these chips continues to rise.

Chen said Singapore has built a complete specialty‑process semiconductor capability over the past decades, and VSMC will build on that foundation. According to the plan, VSMC will focus on 40‑ to 130‑nm specialty processes, targeting a capacity of 44,000 twelve‑inch wafers per month. The products will serve embedded flash memory (eFlash), power‑management and automotive systems, among others.

He added that once VSMC’s capacity is fully ramped, it will significantly boost Singapore’s semiconductor manufacturing strength and further cement Singapore’s role as a trusted node in the global semiconductor supply chain.

The benefits of VSMC extend beyond wafer fabrication; they will also ripple through the broader semiconductor ecosystem, including specialty chemicals and gases, equipment services, plant operations and logistics, creating more opportunities for local suppliers.

Chen stressed that the significance of a major semiconductor investment lies not only in the capital and technology it brings, but also in the industrial capabilities it builds and the development opportunities it creates for local talent.

In terms of manpower, VSMC expects to create 1,600 new jobs, about 75 % of which will be professional, managerial, administrative and technical (PMET) positions such as engineers, chemists and data scientists. These staff will operate advanced manufacturing equipment, develop wafer processes and production, and continuously optimise the manufacturing flow through automation.
Chen said these roles will give Singaporean talent the chance to acquire deep skills in a growing semiconductor industry and build long‑term careers.

Beyond direct job creation, VSMC is expanding collaborations with Singapore’s polytechnics and universities. Chen noted that VSMC recently signed seven memoranda of understanding with local institutes covering internships, graduate recruitment, joint curriculum development, and applied research and innovation projects.

The collaborations will also involve mentorship programmes and industry visits, allowing students early exposure to the semiconductor sector, cultivating skills directly relevant to advanced manufacturing and helping them understand the various career paths within the industry.

Chen added that VSMC participates in Singapore’s talent‑training and industry‑internship programmes and plans to broaden engineering recruitment, helping fresh graduates and mid‑career switchers enter the semiconductor field through structured training and on‑the‑job experience. These initiatives will ensure that as Singapore’s semiconductor industry grows, it translates into high‑quality jobs and long‑term career opportunities, and the government looks forward to VSMC’s continued cooperation with colleges, industry associations and agencies to further strengthen the local talent base.

Looking ahead, Chen said the semiconductor industry is at the start of a new “super‑cycle.” The Singapore government will encourage more related investment to flow into the country and will draw on VSMC’s best practices to help future projects be delivered more quickly.

He noted that in a rapidly expanding semiconductor sector, longer construction times increase opportunity costs, so the government hopes to use VSMC’s experience to enable future investments to “build better and build faster.”

items.title: 債券拋售潮重現！川普拒伊朗方案：10年期殖利率逼近5.2%、油價漲破106美元
items.title_en: Bond Sell‑off Returns as Trump Rejects Iran Deal: 10‑Year Yield Near 5.2%, Oil Prices Rise Above $106
paras: 週一（28日），在美國總統川普拒絕伊朗最新提出的重開荷姆茲海峽方案後，油價上漲，美國公債市場再度遭遇拋售，進一步加劇市場對通膨的疑慮。
根據《彭博》報導，對利率較為敏感的美國2年期公債殖利率上升5個基點至4.90%，10年期殖利率則上升4個基點至5.20%。日本與澳洲公債也同步下跌。
週一美債的拋售延續上週的跌勢，當時聯準會（Fed）官員發表鷹派言論，推動各期美債殖利率升至多年高點。
油市方面，截至台灣時間上午10時59分，布蘭特原油上漲近2%，報每桶106.31美元。伊朗表示不會放寬重開荷姆茲海峽的條件，再度加大聯準會升息以抑制通膨的壓力。
《Axios》則報導，川普雖拒絕德黑蘭最新提案，但表示預期談判將於本週恢復。
Westpac Banking固定收益研究主管Damien McColough表示，聯準會持續釋出的鷹派訊息，加上油價維持在每桶100美元以上，是推動市場看空債券的重要因素。
另一方面，美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）則呼籲聯準會決策官員對利率政策保持「開放態度」。他認為，AI帶來的生產力提升，加上放鬆管制，有助於抑制美國通膨。
利率市場目前預期，聯準會明年可能再升息3次，甚至存在第4次升息的可能。
近期債市走勢也逐漸出現另一項值得關注的訊號。聯準會一連串升息可能開始讓市場敘事轉向美國經濟陷入停滯的風險。
上週，投資人持有10年期美債所要求的額外殖利率，相較於2年期美債殖利率差距一度縮小至17個基點，創2025年初以來最小差距。
這種所謂的殖利率曲線「趨平」，提高10年期美債殖利率即將低於短天期債券殖利率的可能性，而這是市場密切關注的「殖利率曲線倒掛」現象。
《彭博》指出，荷姆茲海峽局勢後續發展，將成為決定債券市場下一步走勢的關鍵。
根據《華爾街日報》報導，談判代表正要求伊朗在核計畫方面作出讓步，以重啟和平談判，並在川普高度重視的議題上安撫川普。
TD Securities駐新加坡亞太利率策略師Prashant Newnaha表示，川普拒絕伊朗提出的外交方案，推動油價再次走高，也對美國公債構成壓力。
他指出，中東談判陷入僵局的情況，可能持續成為市場焦點，直到本週稍晚公布個人消費支出（PCE）物價指數、ISM製造業及服務業數據，以及非農就業報告。
（本文不開放合作夥伴轉載）
paras_en: On Monday (the 28th), after U.S. President Trump rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, oil prices rose and the U.S. Treasury market experienced another wave of selling, further stoking inflation concerns.

According to Bloomberg, the U.S. 2‑year Treasury yield – which is more rate‑sensitive – jumped five basis points to 4.90%, while the 10‑year yield rose four basis points to 5.20%. Japanese and Australian government bonds fell in tandem.
Monday’s Treasury sell‑off continued the decline that began last week when Federal Reserve officials delivered hawkish remarks, pushing yields on all maturities to multi‑year highs.

In the oil market, by 10:59 a.m. Taiwan time Brent crude was up almost 2% at $106.31 a barrel. Iran said it would not relax the conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, adding pressure on the Fed to keep raising rates to curb inflation.
Axios reported that although Trump turned down Tehran’s latest proposal, he expects negotiations to resume later this week.

Westpac Banking fixed‑income research head Damien McColough said the Fed’s continued hawkish messaging, combined with oil staying above $100 a barrel, are key drivers of the market’s bearish stance on bonds.

On the other hand, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Fed policymakers to keep an “open mind” on rate policy, arguing that AI‑driven productivity gains and deregulation can help tame U.S. inflation.
The rate market currently expects the Fed could raise rates three more times next year, with a possible fourth hike also on the table.
Recent bond‑market moves are showing another signal worth watching: a string of Fed hikes may be shifting the market narrative toward the risk of a stalled U.S. economy.
Last week, the extra yield investors demanded for 10‑year Treasuries relative to 2‑year Treasuries narrowed to just 17 basis points, the smallest gap since early 2025.
This so‑called flattening of the yield curve raises the chance that 10‑year yields could fall below short‑term rates – a phenomenon closely watched as a potential yield‑curve inversion.
Bloomberg noted that the evolving situation in the Strait of Hormuz will be a key determinant of the bond market’s next direction.
The Wall Street Journal reported that negotiators are pressing Iran for concessions on its nuclear program to restart peace talks and to address issues that Trump prioritises highly.
TD Securities Asia‑Pacific rates strategist Prashant Newnaha in Singapore said Trump’s rejection of Iran’s diplomatic proposal pushed oil higher again and added pressure on U.S. Treasuries.

He added that the deadlock in Middle‑East talks is likely to remain a market focus until later this week when personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation data, ISM manufacturing and services numbers, and the non‑farm payroll report are released.
